title: Position-based attribution
reading_md:
**What it measures.** How revenue splits when the touch that opened the journey and the touch that closed it get most of the credit. It is also called U-shaped attribution.

**Formula.** For each order, number the touches in the lookback window from 1 to n.

| Touches in the path | Credit |
|---|---|
| 1 | The only touch gets 100% |
| 2 | Each touch gets 50% |
| 3 or more | First touch 40%, last touch 40%, each middle touch 20% / (n - 2) |

A channel's credit is the sum of its touches' shares. Grain: channel × period. Orders with no touch in the window go to an "unattributed" row.

**Worked example.** An order of €500 had the path social → email → display → paid search.

- Social, the first touch: 40% = €200.
- Paid search, the last touch: 40% = €200.
- Email and display share 20% = €100, so €50 each.
- Total: €500.

A one-touch order of €80 gives that touch €80, and a two-touch order of €80 gives €40 to each touch.

**Common mistakes.**

- Using the 40% weights for paths of one or two touches. A one-touch path then gets only 40% of its revenue and a two-touch path 80%, so credit falls short of revenue.
- Splitting the middle 20% by channel instead of by touch.
- Treating 40/20/40 as measured. The weights are a convention someone chose, not an estimate of what each touch caused.

**A note on tools.** Google Ads and GA4 no longer offer position-based attribution, so Voltmarkt computes it from its own touch data.

**How managers ask for it.** "Give credit to both the opener and the closer." "Use a U-shaped model."
